{
  "question_intent": "Request for detailed analysis of bank earnings-call topics",
  "main_topics": ["Investment Banking", "Loan Book Review", "Income vs RWA", "UK Corporate Banking", "Asset Spreads", "Market Share", "Business Expansion", "Client Acquisition", "Business Momentum", "Future Expectations"],
  "answer_completeness": "Complete",
  "response_stance": "Direct",
  "evidence_level": "High",
  "contains_numeric_evidence": true,
  "contains_forward_guidance": false,
  "narrative_alignment": "Aligned",
  "question_quote": "I've got two questions, please. First, on the Investment Banking business. You've done a review of the loan book, so 60% of that is done, and you've seen a 150 basis points pickup in income over RWAs. Firstly, can I ask how much of that pickup is due to maybe more penetration on the income side versus the recycling on the RWA side?",
  "answer_quote": "So the answer is it's a bit of a combination, and we haven't split that out because essentially, what we are doing here is we recognise that two things were true, and they're drawn from, if you like, our historic strength in Fixed Income across Barclays very, very widely. So we're very good at DCM, very good at Lending, probably not as disciplined as we should have been around the returns on that Lending and very focused on getting the initial piece of debt, the RCF and then assuming that we would get subsequent Banking fees to go with us with that, and that would complete the client returns. Clearly, that's quite difficult for us to control. It didn't always happen, which is one of the reasons we pushed more discipline into that business. So, it's not only about reviewing the returns of those loans as they come up for renewal, but also saying what happens then? Either the returns have to improve or we have to broaden the relationship out into Transaction banking. So it's actually a combination of the we see it as one single discussion with the client, which is why we haven't separated it. But we have seen considerable growth in deposit balances. I want to say our dollar deposits are up by about 140%. And that reflects the particular focus we had on, if you like, our US or US nexus clients. So, they might be UK businesses operating in the US, we might have some dollar debt with them. We also want to have some dollar deposits. So, I would say a combination of the two. The remaining 40%, don't think of it as low-hanging fruit. Think of it as literally the things that came up for renewal during that period. Roughly, the loans have a three-year average life. So, there's no reason to expect that the remaining year will be different to the first two is the way I would think about it. In terms of UK Corporate Banking, so what we haven't seen there is a compression in asset spreads. And from our perspective, it's really because we were coming from way behind. So, we are still considerably below our natural market share in that business. So, our loan-to-deposit ratio is 34%. If you look at our peers, it's going to be anywhere between 55% and 80%. So, we're coming from a really different position. And all we've done is created an expectation that we would lend with the regional teams and improve the process. Now clearly, we would expect to see some momentum there also coming from the fact that we're consolidating everything onto one platform from five in the shape of Portal. But as I look, I'm really happy to see the growth. They've grown their income in the fourth quarter by 18% from lending. We've seen about 100 basis point pickup in market share. I'm really happy about that, but I'm just as focused on the RoTE, which means there's two things that matter. The first is the default grade. The second is the margin. And neither of those two things are moving relative to the portfolio. So, this is not an expansion driven by pricing and risk. It's an expansion driven by capability and willingness to lend with clients we already have in the door. And indeed, going out and getting new clients. So, we've got, I think, more than 1,100 new clients in just two years. So, the business has some momentum now that it has not had for years. And actually, as I look sort of further out in the plan, one of the areas where I think probably consensus and our expectations are a little bit departing is probably the corporate business.",
  "reason": "The response provides a direct answer to the question, with high evidence level including numeric evidence and a clear narrative alignment with the question's intent. All requested keys are present and correctly filled."
}
